results.brief_description:

Shows the nature of white light by experiments involving the dispersion and re-combination of colours of the spectrum. Illustrates the nature of colour by demonstrations showing the reflection, transmission and absorption of colour.

results.title: The Nature and development of affection
results.brief_description: An experiment with chimpanzees. One animal is placed in a compartment with a wired cage source of milk, a “wire mother”, another is placed with a similar wire source of milk but this is covered with a furry material and is known as the “cloth mother”. Experiments contrast the social behaviour and the amount of affection which grows with each animal and “mother”. Towards the end a human baby is shown to be attracted to a cloth mother. The University of Wisonsin Department of Psychology, Primate Laboratory with Dr. Harry F. Harlow.

results.title: The Nature & nurture of development:Pt I
results.creator_credit: Darrel Schwandt, George A. Colburn, DLGHS and GPN
results.brief_description:
Episode number 23 of Series “The Worlds of childhood”.
Shows how development always occurs in context and that time and place are important in child development, together with biology. This program examines what has been learnt from recent research and considers moral development and the effects of environment in the nature/nurture controversy.

results.title: The Nature & nurture of development: Pt II
results.creator_credit: Darrel Schwandt, George A. Colburn, DLGHS and GPN
results.brief_description:
Episode number 24 of Series “The Worlds of childhood”.
Shows how development always occurs in context and that time and place are important in child development, together with biology. This program considers childhood rites of passage and acculturisation. It also presents a review of topics such as mental agility, physical growth, language and personality development.

results.title: The Natural world: the witness was a fly
results.brief_description: Narrated by Dr Zakaria Erzinclioglu who specialises in using flies as a means of crime detection in forensic science, this program profiles actual cases across the globe and interviews experts in the field to illustrate how the evidence of plants, animals and nature have proven or disproven cases. It takes an in depth look at the procedures and testing that takes place in the laboratories and outlines what different plants, animals and insects can offer in solving crime.

results.title: The Nativity
results.creator_credit: Dudley Shaw Ashton and Samaritan Films
results.brief_description: The famous painting of the “Nativity” by Piero della Francesca (1416-1492) is in the collection of the National Gallery, London. Sir Philip Hendy talks about the painting which is seen alone, as a whole and in detail, without any other effects. The “Nativity” was among della Francesca’s last pictures, executed shortly before he gave up painting due to failing eyesight. Its unfinished appearance is due to harsh restoration of a later period. Narrated by Sir Philip Handy.

results.title: The National parks of Canada
results.brief_description: Where once there was only Banff, the number of National Parks across Canada now approaches thirty, in accordance with the federal government’s policy of setting aside scenic tracts of land for the enjoyment of present and future generations. This film shows them all. In a coast-to-coast tour it locates each one on a map and shows the scenic features and recreational facilities that each one offers. Sound film without words.
